outcomes.text: Name the foods in the starchy group: bread, rice, potatoes, pasta, flour and cereals.
Name fresh, frozen, dried, canned and juiced fruit and vegetables, and dairy foods: milk, cream, cheese and yoghurt.
Name the protein foods: meat, fish, eggs, beans, nuts, seeds and alternatives like Quorn, TVP and tofu.
Name the foods and drinks high in fat and/or sugar: butter, spreads, oils, sugar and syrup.
Explain the importance of a healthy diet.
Use the commodity groups to make balanced food choices.
Apply the eight tips for healthy eating and current government guidelines.
Describe obesity, cardiovascular disease and coronary heart disease.
Describe diabetes, diverticulitis, osteoporosis, dental health, anaemia and high blood pressure in relation to diet.

topics.title: 2 Nutritional and dietary needs of different groups

outcomes.text: Plan balanced food, nutrients and portion sizes for babies, toddlers, pre-school and school-aged children.
Plan balanced food, nutrients and portion sizes for adolescents, adults, older people, and pregnant and lactating women.
Identify foods that may cause allergic reactions.
Describe lactose and gluten intolerance (coeliac disease).

subtopics.title: Dietary reference values and nutritional analysis

outcomes.text: Use dietary reference values for recommended daily amounts of macro and micronutrients and energy.
Plan recipes, meals and diets from nutritional analysis.
Modify recipes to meet dietary guidelines by substituting ingredients, changing the cooking method and changing portion size.
Explain BMR and PAL and their importance in determining energy requirements.
Link food intake and activity to maintaining a healthy body weight through life.
Explain factors affecting energy needs: gender, life stage, pregnancy, size, genetics, occupation and lifestyle.
Describe deficiency and excess of energy.
Name energy sources: protein, fat, carbohydrate and alcohol.
Use kcal and kJ and the recommended percentage of daily energy intake, and calculate energy values.
Describe high and low biological value protein and its structure.
Describe protein's functions and deficiency.
Name animal and vegetable protein sources.
Describe types of fats and oils: saturated, unsaturated and polyunsaturated.
Describe fat's functions and deficiency.
Name animal and vegetable, visible and invisible, fat sources.
Describe sugars (mono- and disaccharides), starch as complex carbohydrate, and fibre.
Describe carbohydrate's functions and deficiency.
Name sources of sugar, starch and fibre.
Describe vitamins A (retinol, carotene), D, E and K: functions, deficiency and food sources.
Describe B1, B2, B3 and B9 (folate): functions, deficiency and food sources.
Describe B12 and vitamin C (ascorbic acid): functions, deficiency and food sources.
Describe calcium, iron, sodium, fluoride, iodine and phosphorus: functions and deficiency.
Name the foods that supply these minerals.
Describe water's functions and deficiency.
State the recommended daily intake and the sources and foods that supply water.

topics.title: 11 Nutritional content of the main commodity groups

outcomes.text: Describe the nutritional content of starchy foods, and fruit and vegetables.
Describe the nutritional content of milk and dairy foods, and protein foods.
Describe the nutritional content of foods and drinks high in fat and/or sugar.

units.title: Section B: Food (food provenance and food choice)

outcomes.text: Compare local and seasonal foods and organic versus non-organic farming.
Classify fruits and vegetables.
Describe intensive and free-range rearing, and classify meat, poultry and game.
Describe how fish are caught, sustainable supply and fish classification.
Describe how wheat is milled to flour and how milk is heat treated.
Describe how raw food is processed into a food product.
Describe how milk makes butter, cream, yoghurt and cheese, and how flour makes bread and pasta.
Explain high-temperature methods: pasteurisation, sterilisation, UHT and canning.
Explain chilling, freezing, cook-freeze, blast chilling and accelerated freeze-drying.
Explain drying, smoking, and preserving with acids, salt and sugar.
Explain controlled and modified atmosphere packaging and vacuum packing.
Explain food availability, access and utilisation, and food security's impact on society and markets.
Explain how Fairtrade affects producers and workers, and ethical issues of GM food.
Explain environmental issues of food waste, carbon footprint, transport and sustainability of resources.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of fortification.
Describe additives: preservatives, colourings, flavourings, sweeteners, emulsifiers, stabilisers, thickeners and antioxidants.
Describe probiotics and prebiotics.
Recognise traditional ingredients of British cuisine and at least two international cuisines.
Explain religious or cultural factors, traditional methods, presentation and eating patterns.
Explain how traditional recipes have been adapted to today's society.
Explain personal, social, economic and medical factors, including cost, preference, seasonality and occasion.
Explain consumer information, food labelling and marketing.
Explain how Buddhism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Rastafarianism and Sikhism affect food choice.
Explain vegetarian types, animal welfare, local produce and organic food as ethical choices.

units.title: Section C: Cooking and food preparation

subtopics.title: Why and how food is cooked

outcomes.text: Explain why food is cooked: safety, digestibility and palatability.
Explain heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation.
Explain how preparation and cooking affect nutritional value and sensory properties.
Explain gelatinisation, dextrinisation and caramelisation of carbohydrates.
Explain shortening, aeration, plasticity and emulsification of fats and oils.
Explain coagulation, foam formation, gluten formation and acid denaturation of protein.
Explain enzymic browning in fruit and vegetables.
Explain raising agents: yeast, chemical agents, air and steam.
Describe changes in texture, appearance, colour, taste, sound and aroma when food is cooked.
Explain sight, taste, touch, smell and hearing in food choice, and the five basic tastes including umami.
Set up a testing panel.
Use rating, ranking and profiling systems with suitable descriptive terms.
Explain the role of time, temperature, moisture and food in bacterial growth, and mould and yeast growth.
Recognise signs of spoilage: natural decay, enzyme action and yeast.
Describe helpful micro-organisms in food production.

subtopics.title: Safe handling from shop to table

outcomes.text: Buy food safely using labels, date marks, visual checks and reputable suppliers.
Store food correctly in the right types of storage.
Prevent direct and indirect cross-contamination and food poisoning.
Cook and serve safely, handling high-risk foods and critical temperatures.
Weigh and measure liquids and solids accurately, and grease, line and flour tins evenly.
Choose and adjust cooking process and time, and test for readiness.
Use specialist equipment and explain ingredient functions in basic recipes.
Fillet, portion and slice meat, fish and alternatives evenly.
Use bridge hold and claw grip to peel, slice, dice and cut fruit and vegetables into batons and julienne.
Tenderise and marinate with acids and flavourings.
Roll, wrap, skewer, coat, layer and shape meat, fish and alternatives, preventing cross-contamination.
Prepare fruit and vegetables by mashing, grating, blanching, piping, juicing and garnishing, controlling browning and spoilage.
Use water-based hob methods: steaming, boiling, simmering, blanching and poaching.
Use dry heat and fat methods: dry-frying, shallow frying and stir-frying.
Use the grill and the oven: baking, roasting, casseroles, tagines and braising.
Make a blended white sauce and show how liquid:starch ratio affects viscosity.
Make a reduction sauce and show how evaporation concentrates flavour.
Make a stabilised emulsion sauce such as dressing, mayonnaise or hollandaise.
Set a mixture by gelation, using starch on chilling.
Set a mixture by coagulation, using protein on heating.
Whisk egg for a gas-in-air foam.
Use chemical raising agents such as self-raising flour and baking powder.
Use steam as a raising agent in choux pastry and batter.
Use shortening, gluten formation and fermentation (proving) for bread, pastry and pasta.
Roll pastry, use a pasta machine, create layers and rest dough.
Glaze and finish choux, rolls, pasta, flat breads, pinwheels, pizza and calzone.
Taste and season during cooking and change taste and aroma with infusions, herbs, spices, pastes, jus and reductions.
Change texture and flavour through browning, glazing, crusts and crumbs.
Use garnishes, food styling, portioning and presentation.
